title: sdk: add typed stream-safety guards, cross-sdk backoff shim, and coordinated version bumps
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Different SDKs had subtly divergent streaming semantics and retry behaviors which caused hard-to-debug client edge-cases (double-cancel, lost error events, and inconsistent backoff telemetry). This PR introduces small, opt-in typed guards and a tiny cross-SDK backoff shim to align runtime behavior and improve ergonomics when consumers migrate between Python/TS/Go.

Summary of changes: 1) Add typed stream-safety guards: a lightweight consumer-side guard that enforces single-terminal event semantics (only one of close/error) and surfaces a consistent error envelope across languages. Implementations: TypeScript guard + tests (sdk/typescript), Go guard + tests (sdk/go), Python wrapper with typing annotations and context-manager helper (sdk/python). 2) Cross-SDK backoff shim: a small, language-agnostic policy spec serialized as JSON in the SDK root; SDKs adopt the shim to produce identical retry timing and telemetry tags for the most common transient errors (auth refresh, 429, connection reset). 3) Ergonomic minor API change: introduce Stream.cancel(reason: str|None) / Stream.close() parity doc and deprecation shim (old cancel() still available for one release). 4) Coordinated version bumps and changelog updates: python 2.4.1 -> 2.5.0, typescript 3.1.0 -> 3.2.0, go v0.9.7 -> v0.10.0.

Checklist: - [x] Implement TS guard and unit tests - [x] Implement Go guard and unit tests - [x] Implement Python wrapper, typing and integration tests - [x] Add shared backoff JSON and normalization code in each SDK - [x] Update SDK changelogs and release manifest - [x] Run cross-language integration matrix in CI - [x] Docs: streaming best-practices and migration note

Testing and rollout: Local integration matrix exercised against the hosted QA runtime (stream smoke, auth refresh fault-injection, and 429 storms). CI initially flagged a flaky Go race in the stream test; reproduced locally and fixed by a short mutex around the internal state transition. After fix the full matrix passed. Rollout plan: merge to main and publish SDKs in a coordinated window; leave deprecation shim for one release and call out migration in the changelog and docs site.

Notes: The changes are intentionally small and additive. Consumers that rely on the old multi-terminal behavior should not break immediately due to the guard being opt-in via an instantiation flag (enable_stream_safety=true) for the first release; we plan to enable it by default in next minor once telemetry shows insignificant breakage.

release_notes: Add opt-in stream safety guards to TS/Go/Python SDKs; introduce standardized cross-SDK backoff policy; minor ergonomic parity for Stream.cancel/close; coordinated SDK version bumps (python 2.5.0, typescript 3.2.0, go v0.10.0). Migration: enable_stream_safety is opt-in for 2.5/3.2/0.10; enable by default in the next minor release after monitoring. See docs/sdk/streaming-migration.md for migration steps and examples.
notes: Backport readiness: change is additive and small; mark as backport-ready for any stable release branches if needed. Telemetry: tag redwood.telemetry.stream_guard=enabled for consumers that opt in.
